FINDING_ID: LB_F001

FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.66  
DESCRIPTION: In [_admissibility_mask()](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L805), the line `self.role_map.get(model.model_id, Role.PAR)` silently treats any model missing from `role_map` as a normal participant. Because [LoadBalancer.__init__()](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L790) never validates that every live model has an explicit role, an unclassified model can receive work. I verified this with three models and `role_map={'pm': PM, 'worker': PAR}`: the unassigned model `ghost` was marked admissible and got the task. That breaks the role-allocation contract; missing metadata should not grant execution rights.  
PROPOSED_FIX: In `LoadBalancer.__init__`, require exact set equality between `self.models` and `role_map` keys for the active pool, and raise on missing or extra IDs. In `_admissibility_mask`, remove the `Role.PAR` default and treat unknown models as an error.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: LB_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.83  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.62  
DESCRIPTION: In [RoleAssignment.reassign()](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L517), `best_col_id = max(col_scores, key=lambda mid: col_scores[mid])` drops the deterministic tie-break used by `assign()`. `col_scores` is built from `active_models`, which is a `set`, so when adjusted COL scores tie and there is no active `current_col`, the winner depends on hash iteration order rather than model quality. I verified this by running the same reassignment under different `PYTHONHASHSEED` values with identical candidates `a` and `b`: some seeds picked `a`, others picked `b`. That makes COL reassignment non-reproducible.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Use a deterministic ranking identical to `assign()`, for example sorting candidates by `(col_score, _tie_break_key(model), model_id)` descending, and derive candidate order from `self._models` rather than a set.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: LB_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.80  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.57  
DESCRIPTION: The load-balancing layer never enforces unique `model_id` or `task_id`, but several paths assume uniqueness. In [RoleAssignment.assign()](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L471), [LoadBalancer.__init__()](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L801), and [Allocation](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L724), dicts and `list.index()` collapse duplicates silently. I verified two concrete failures: with duplicate `task_id='t'`, `Allocation.model_load()` counted `1000 + 2000` as `4000` because `{t.task_id: t}` kept only the second task; with duplicate `model_id='m'`, an assignment in the second matrix column became invisible and `model_load_fraction('m', ...)` returned `0.0`. This is silent state corruption, not just a poor error message.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Enforce uniqueness of `model_id` and `task_id` at construction time in `RoleAssignment.assign`, `LoadBalancer.__init__`, and an `Allocation.__post_init__`, and fail fast on duplicates.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: LB_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.74  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.49  
DESCRIPTION: [DynamicManagementConfig.__post_init__()](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L199) still leaves several Area-2 parameters effectively unchecked. `epsilon_bal`, `lambda_lat`, `lambda_bal`, `tau_moderate`, and `tau_critical` can all take nonsensical values even though they directly define load-balancing semantics. I verified that `DynamicManagementConfig(epsilon_bal=-0.1)` is accepted, and then a perfectly even 2-way split reports `balanced=False`; negative `lambda_bal` and `lambda_lat` are also accepted, which inverts the meaning of the objective. This allows invalid allocator states before any task is solved.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add explicit bounds checks for Area-2 parameters: `epsilon_bal >= 0`, `lambda_lat >= 0`, `lambda_bal >= 0`, `0 <= tau_moderate <= 1`, `0 <= tau_critical <= 1`, plus the existing ordering rule `tau_moderate <= tau_critical`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE
